findings.title: Curmudgeon reviews 1 fresh WIN/run x 1 run/day; win-new not batchable
findings.evidence: curmudgeon.md:72 ('Full stop after one queue item'), :160 ('review ONE queue item per run'), :243 Step 8a gate 5 (win-new always singleton); cron dome-curmudgeon '0 2 * * *' = 1/day
findings.burst_impact: 3 WINs need >=3 curmudgeon days for first-pass review; +1 day because curmudgeon (01:05 UTC) precedes decider (02:03 UTC) on detection day. Full burst clears first-review+first-patch ~Day 5-6 at quiet cadence vs ~1 day at reverted 3-slot.

findings.title: Quiet-period throttle (cadence cuts + verify pause) has no burst-triggered un-throttle — RANK 1
findings.evidence: task descriptions 'REVERT ... if dome breaks drought' (manual); curmudgeon-verify 'Re-enable when verify-class items appear' (manual); poller detects WINs but touches no cadence
findings.burst_impact: Root cause of WL-1 and WL-4 recovery latency. Burst crawls at 1/day until a human notices and flips 3 crons + re-enables verify. Recovery is purely detection-latency-bound.

findings.burst_impact: Under burst poller is slower (more changes/ work) exactly when analyst needs its output; stale status.json read can skip Mode 0 for a full day. Self-heals next day via GitHub raw-count curl — latency, not data loss.

is_tinker_the_weak_link: No on capacity (quiet period, Opus, ample quota). But tinker once/day has up to 24h detection latency, worse than poller's same-cycle detection. Tinker is the right escalation/fallback surface (owns PROP-030 backlog-trend pre-flight + latest-tinker-summary.txt) but poller is the right PRIMARY detector. This shaped PROP-117's two-detector design.
